assumptions: OpenTsiolkovsky 1.0.0 (MIT, external binary -- not vendored; see NOTICE; openTsiolkovsky-v1.0.0-<platform>.tar.gz, pinned per-platform SHA-256 digests live in scripts/fetch_opentsiolkovsky.py)
OT pos_eci_*/vel_eci_* read as LAUNCH_ECI (axes = ECEF at the launch epoch, held inertial) and converted to GCRS by orbitopt.flightlab.frames.to_gcrs at the epoch
created_utc is the mission epoch: this adapter is a pure function of (target, vehicle, attitude program), so repeated calls write byte-identical runs

vehicle: Hand-tuned two-stage demonstrator sized for a ~400 km / 51.6 deg insertion from LC-39A within the FL scenario constraints (max_q 60 kPa, 5 g); the single-burn cutoff leaves ~130 km of apogee above perigee -- closing the circle is E2 optimizer headroom, not a vehicle defect.
vehicle: Stage separation and engine restart follow a Falcon-9-style sequence; the stage-1 throttle-down near MECO keeps thrust acceleration under 5 g; aero is a generic tube-and-fins guess.
target: Synthetic two-stage vehicle; masses/engines are illustrative placeholders, not real performance figures.
target: Max-Q and max-acceleration limits are design assumptions, not certified vehicle structural limits.
orbit re-fly: not requested (physics_verified stays None = not assessed)
Gate-B verdict (FL-006): orbitopt.flightlab.checks.evaluate -- the three verification booleans are independent; None means not assessed, never passed
